title: When Semantic Segmentation Meets Frequency Aliasing
mechanism: De-aliasing filter zeroes feature-map frequencies above the equivalent Nyquist frequency before each downsampling (parameter free); FreqMix learns channel x spatial weights for below/above-Nyquist bands inside encoder blocks.
adaptation: Put DAF before the ResNet-34 max-pool and the stride-2 convs of layer2/3/4 (not before conv1, so stride-2 skips keep crack detail); FreqMix in layer1/2. EL fingers (pitch likely 4 to 6 px at 512, unverified) alias into moire from stride 4 onward; moire depends on source rescaling, a plausible cause of BMRK and E1 weakness. Keeps ImageNet weights.
min_experiment: Arm: house + DAF + FreqMix; baseline house and PF; 5 seeds, CV then test/E1; metrics crack IoU, relF1@2, per-source crack IoU, E1 relF1@2; kill if crack IoU < +0.012 and E1 relF1@2 < +0.02. Precede with a 1 h CPU diagnostic of finger pitch and encoder aliasing score.
evidence: R: UPerNet-R50 Cityscapes 78.1 to 79.7 mIoU, boundary IoU 61.8 to 63.2; PASCAL VOC 74.3 to 76.1; ADE20K 38.9 to 40.4. Large datasets, not thin structures.
prior_overlap: none; section 5 never varied downsampling or anti-aliasing. 2x resolution n.d. is a different mechanism (compute, not aliasing).
